claim: Declares which elements are cel-shaded 3D instead of drawn, from a single prop up to a fully CG shot. Modern anime mixes constantly, and stating the mix is the only way the 2D and 3D halves can be made to match instead of fighting. camera_3d is a motion option and renders as the baseline.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: cg prop, 3d model object, cel shaded
cg vehicle, 3d model car, cel shaded
cg crowd, 3d model background characters, cel shaded
cg environment, 3d model background, cel shaded

review.issue: "none" and "camera_3d" both have empty clauses - two identical baseline panels in one card. Beyond that, SDXL cannot scope a render style to one named object: "cg prop, 3d model object, cel shaded", "cg vehicle...", "cg crowd...", "cg environment..." will each push the whole frame toward 3DCG, so the four scoped options plus full_3dcg largely converge. "cel shaded" also does no work here - it is what an anime checkpoint already draws.
review.fix: Mark camera_3d renderable:false per-option. For the rest, hang the 3d tag on the element and drop the dead "cel shaded" token - e.g. crowd_3d "3d, cg crowd, mmd background characters", environment_3d "3d background, cg scenery" - and expect props_3d/vehicles_3d to bleed globally. vehicles_3d additionally has no referent in the subject sentence (there is no vehicle in a soccer stadium), so it will either force an incongruous car onto the pitch or be ignored; consider dropping it.
